items.name: Tenant / data-isolation leak
items.class: broken access control / tenant leak (OWASP #1 / IDOR)
items.exact_change: Replaced the user-scoped member lookup `@conversation = current_user.conversations.find(params[:id])` with the unscoped `@conversation = Conversation.find(params[:id])`. The two-line comment advertising the scoping was rewritten to a neutral routing comment (semantic parity; no comment names the vuln).
items.routed_path_evidence: before_action :set_conversation, only: %i[show destroy] (conversations_controller.rb:2); routes.rb `resources :conversations` => GET/DELETE /conversations/:id (show, destroy). index (line 5), create/new, the nested MessagesController#set_conversation (messages_controller.rb:26 `current_user.conversations.find(params[:conversation_id])`) and the sidebar (application_controller.rb:16) stay scoped => subtle.
items.live_verify: ruby -c => Syntax OK. Member lookup now resolves an UNSCOPED Conversation.find. Gate-4 live-exploit evidence: the model's own system test test/system/authorization_test.rb:12-16 ('a user cannot open the conversation of somebody else') signs in as alice (setup:9) and visits conversation_path(conversations(:private_notes)) which belongs to bob (fixtures/conversations.yml private_notes.user=bob) expecting 404 — the unscoped find now returns bob's conversation (200/show), reddening that assertion (and the sibling destroy path). This is valid live proof per PROTOCOL gate #4, not a build break.
items.fairness_note: This model guards the tenant path with a cross-user 404 system spec, so the Critical leak cannot be placed green — identical to the qwen38_flash and deepseek_v4_1_flash precedents. The messages path is left scoped (its own specs stay green); no test is gutted (test-defang is item #6, a later boundary). #1 is thus likely caught at sprint 3 via the model's own red spec — credit the model's test discipline.

items.name: Removed login link / nav regression
items.file_line:
app/views/registrations/new.html.erb:37-40 (removed the trailing `

Already have an account? <%= link_to "Sign in", sign_in_path %>

` block)
items.exact_change: Deleted the only navigational affordance pointing to the sign-in page. Removed the 4-line paragraph block containing `link_to "Sign in", sign_in_path`.
items.routed_path_evidence: registrations/new is the rendered sign-up page (routes.rb `get "sign_up" => "registrations#new"`). The layout (layouts/application.html.erb) renders no nav; the sidebar (_sidebar.html.erb) is shown only to authenticated users and links to conversations/account/Sign out; the sign-in page (sessions/new) only holds its own form. After removal, `grep -rniE sign_in_path app/views/` returns only sessions/new.html.erb:7 — the sign-in page's OWN form action, not a navigation link. A logged-out visitor on the sign-up page has no visible way to reach sign-in.
items.live_verify: Stays GREEN (intended: the model lacks a test guarding this link). The sign-in system tests reach the form via `visit sign_in_path` directly (application_system_test_case.rb:21 sign_in_as helper; authentication_test.rb:25,46; account_test.rb) — none clicks the registration-page link. authentication_test.rb:20 `assert_text "Sign in"` after Sign-out is satisfied by the sessions/new page's own `Sign in` heading, not by the removed link. App still boots.
items.adaptation: none (primary target present; byte-equivalent placement to qwen38_flash / deepseek_v4_1_flash precedents)

items.name: Pinned vulnerable dependency
items.exact_change: Gemfile: `gem "puma", ">= 5.0"` -> `gem "puma", "6.4.1"` (+ neutral rollback comment). Gemfile.lock: GEM spec `puma (8.0.2)` -> `puma (6.4.1)` (dependency `nio4r (~> 2.0)` preserved); DEPENDENCIES `puma (>= 5.0)` -> `puma (= 6.4.1)`; CHECKSUMS `puma (8.0.2) sha256=c8ed871d...` line dropped (hand-edited-pin look).
items.routed_path_evidence: Editing the real Gemfile/Gemfile.lock IS the real code path (naturally-additive case per PROTOCOL §1). puma 6.4.1 is affected by CVE-2024-21647 (HTTP request smuggling, fixed 6.4.2). The app ships `bundler-audit` in its own dev/test group (Gemfile:48) so the pin is on the app's own audit path.
items.live_verify: `bundle lock --local --print` resolved cleanly (exit 0); the printed in-memory graph pins puma (6.4.1) at spec/DEPENDENCIES/CHECKSUMS. On-disk Gemfile.lock md5 verified UNCHANGED by the check (d1d42053...). No reverse dependency requires puma > 6.4.1 (only the top-level pin); nio4r (~> 2.0) stays valid for 6.4.1.
items.adaptation: ADAPTED. Catalog default #3 is `devise 4.7.0` if devise used, else `nokogiri 1.13.5`. This app has NO devise (hand-rolled auth) => devise pin N/A. nokogiri 1.13.5 is UNRESOLVABLE here: rails-html-sanitizer (1.7.1) requires `nokogiri (>= 1.15.7, != 1.16.x...)`, so a 1.13.5 pin makes the lock internally unresolvable. Per the catalog equivalent-target rule I used the established strong-alternate parity substitution `puma 6.4.1` (CVE-2024-21647), which satisfies every lock constraint — same choice as the qwen38_flash and deepseek_v4_1_flash precedents. Severity recorded High 3 (uniform; denominator-40 parity preserved).
